ObjectName.value: Historic heritage sites of Gujarat with GPS coordinates

Categories.value: Temples in Gujarat|Hindu temples in Gujarat|Tourism in Gujarat|Caves of Gujarat|Jain temples in Gujarat|Self-published work|Locator maps of Gujarat|ODbL OpenStreetMap|Historic sites in India

ImageDescription.value:
Gujarat is a western state of India. With Harappan civilization sites such as Lothal, it is home to some of the oldest historic sites (2500 BCE to 2000 BCE) in India. While most historic sites relate to Hinduism, the state also hosts a large number of sites related to Jainism. A few Buddhist sites are also found dated between 3rd century BCE and 11th century CE. These sites show signs of natural erosion as well as deliberate vandalism and destruction. After the 13th century, Gujarat became home to notable monuments related to Islam some built from ruined parts of lost Hindu and Jain temples.

Gujarat monuments attest to highly sophisticated designs, architectural plans and intricate artwork. These include caves, temples, step wells (vav) and others – predominantly following the square-circle principles of Indian architecture found in Sanskrit manuscripts.

The map above shows over 200 historic sites in Gujarat with GPS coordinates. These are predominantly Hindu and Jain sites. The GPS coordinates are based on actual field survey and periodic site visits since 2011 for detailed aerial and surface photography along with architectural plans digitization effort.
